hypothesis: A predeclared asymmetric portfolio that permits HYPE breakout long, ETH precompression-pullback long, and SOL range-onset long and short may improve after-friction shared-capital performance over enabling every source symmetrically on both sides.
decision: Keep the asymmetric shared-portfolio hypothesis active as a report-only candidate and begin prospective scoring from the revision-1 declaration time. The bounded observer is operational and currently has zero qualifying post-cutoff resolved lifecycles, so it makes no new profitability claim. It separately reports HYPE-short and ETH-short controls, excludes pre-cutoff and open lifecycles, and leaves live v25 unchanged.
falsifier: The observer contract is invalidated by accepting a pre-cutoff entry, an open mark, a mismatched profile, a malformed lifecycle, or a side outside the frozen route map; by claiming counterfactual fills or capital reallocation; or by gaining execution authority. The portfolio hypothesis weakens if new after-friction candidate lifecycles become nonpositive, lose their advantage over the separately reported symmetric controls, or remain dependent on one winner.
limitations: No qualifying post-cutoff lifecycle has resolved, so this revision does not update the profitability estimate.
The running v25 router may allocate capital differently from the frozen candidate and can displace otherwise eligible opportunities.
Only actual resolved venue lifecycles are scored; missed and unfilled opportunities are not simulated.
Excluded HYPE-short and ETH-short lifecycles are descriptive controls and cannot be interpreted as losses the candidate would certainly have avoided.
Open BTC, ETH, and SPCX marks at initialization remain provisional and are excluded.
The observer does not modify the live profile, order routing, size, leverage, stops, targets, exits, or transition state.
